sub: A unique number and an NFC object that opens it. One tap — nothing to install.
problem_title:
Information still travels
on paper and out loud.
problems: Company bank details are written out by hand. One wrong digit and the payment lands in the wrong account.
A car is blocking the way. There is no number behind the glass, or there is one, on a scrap of paper.
Nothing on the collar. Whoever finds the animal has no way to reach its owner.
A bag, a key, a suitcase — found, and still it never gets back to anyone.
The card number is read out loud or written down. That is where both the errors and the risk are.
Nothing to exchange at a meeting
The cards run out, typing a number takes too long, and afterwards nobody can find anybody.
A small brand is hard to remember
The name never stays on the customer's phone. Every time you start the introduction again.
A PDF goes out, the link is lost, versions drift. The employer opens the oldest one.
solution_title: One tap, and the page opens.
solution: Three letters and three digits — MYN042 — become an address, and it is yours for life.
A card, a ring, a bracelet, or a tag on a table. An NFC chip and a QR code inside.
The guest taps their own phone and it opens in their own language. Nobody installs anything.

design_body: The owner picks the card design, and every one of them is drawn by us rather than borrowed. A low serial number cannot be reproduced at all — which is the one thing on the card that is genuinely scarce.

model_side: Individuals pay by card through Payme. Venues and companies pay by invoice and bank transfer, which is how a business here actually pays.
math_title: Recurring revenue, at the smallest band.
math_note: At the entry band of 149,000 UZS and nothing above it — a hotel or a larger restaurant pays twice that. Devices and personal numbers are not counted here at all. These are venue counts, not a market size.
why_title: Three things are true at once.
why: Every phone sold in recent years reads NFC, and after 2020 a QR code on a table needs no explaining to anyone.
Cafes and hotels no longer compete on price alone. How fast somebody answers a table is a thing guests notice.
Payme and bank transfer make a monthly subscription collectable from a business — what turns this from a gadget into revenue.

notplain_title: This is not an ordinary NFC card.
notplain_body: There are plenty of NFC cards. The difference is not the card — it is what stands behind it.
notplain: A unique number in the AAA000 format. A low serial cannot be reproduced — nobody else can print it.

New job, new number, new company: you edit the page. The card stays the card.
